title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
authors: Jiaxin Wu, Hongzhuo Wu, Zuhong Zhang, Xiaoyu Guan, Jinbo Zhao, Yuting Guo
abstract: Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl- induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between -40 and 85 degrees C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: Hierarchical multipoint anchoring strengthens buried interfaces in inverted perovskite solar cells, improving efficiency and resistance to thermal cycling.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Engineering stronger transparent-conductive-oxide/SAM interfaces addresses stress-driven adhesion failure that limits device durability under temperature fluctuations.

title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements
authors: Nabanita Sarker, Hafiz Imtiaz
abstract: Machine learning coupled with device simulation is widely used to optimize thin-film solar cells, but almost exclusively in the forward direction, from device parameters to predicted performance. The inverse problem encountered after fabrication, namely identifying the mechanism that limits a given device, is still addressed by manual inspection of characterization data. In this work, both directions are examined for lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells using approximately 42,000 SCAPS-1D simulations. Replacing the Spiro-OMeTAD hole transport layer with CuI increases the simulated power conversion efficiency from 19.6\% to 21.6\%, almost entirely through the fill factor. Surrogate models trained and tested on a factorial parameter grid substantially overstate their predictive accuracy. An XGBoost regressor attains $R^2 = 0.9997$ on held-out grid points but only 0.58 on independently sampled devices, whereas training on a Latin hypercube design of comparable size restores $R^2 = 0.995$. For the inverse problem, a multi-label classifier identifies which of six degradation mechanisms are present from simulated temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit-voltage measurements. It achieves a macro $F_1$ score of 0.938, compared to 0.687 for a calibrated physics-rule baseline. The classifier does not, however, generalize to combinations of mechanisms absent from the training set.

infographic.key_insight: Machine learning can diagnose simulated degradation mechanisms in lead-free RbSn₀.₅Ge₀.₅I₃ solar cells, but strong test scores do not guarantee generalization.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Replacing Spiro-OMeTAD with CuI raises simulated efficiency from 19.6% to 21.6%, mainly by improving fill factor.

title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
authors: Kentaro Nakajo, Hojun Im, Keiichiro Nishimura, Masahiro Teraoka, Masaya Kikuchi
abstract: While graphene/n-type silicon (Gr/n-Si) and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si solar cells offer a cost-effective alternative to conventional photovoltaics, achieving simultaneous high power conversion efficiency (PCE) and long-term environmental stability remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report the synergistic enhancement of both performance and stability in a planar trilayer PEDOT:PSS/Gr/n-Si Schottky junction architecture. By systematically benchmarking this hybrid device against pristine Gr/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells fabricated on untextured substrates, we isolate the fundamental optoelectronic and barrier functions of the carbon lattice. Comprehensive analyses reveal that the PEDOT:PSS layer simultaneously functions as an anti-reflection coating, a moderate p-type dopant for the underlying graphene, and a conductivity enhancer, collectively optimizing interfacial charge transport. Consequently, the trilayer device achieves a PCE of 8.52%, markedly outperforming the pristine Gr/n-Si reference cell (4.56%). Crucially, the atomic impermeability of the graphene sheet serves as a robust environmental barrier. While bare PEDOT:PSS/n-Si junctions retained only ~29% of their initial efficiency after 75 days of ambient exposure, graphene shields the active junction from moisture-induced degradation of the hygroscopic PEDOT:PSS overlayer. This enables the trilayer device to retain approximately 90% of its initial efficiency over the same 75-day period. The complementary roles of graphene as both a highly crystalline charge transport interface and an impermeable protective barrier establish a highly effective strategy for engineering high-efficiency, environmentally stable hybrid photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si trilayer combines improved solar-cell efficiency with graphene-enabled protection against ambient degradation.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This planar architecture offers a route to more efficient and durable hybrid silicon photovoltaics without substrate texturing.

title: Evidence-grounded large language models guide perovskite solar cell design and optimization
authors: YanKai Chen, Zhi Wan, ZiHao Li, Tao Jing
abstract: Using large language models to interpret experimental evidence, design discriminating experiments and formulate well-supported mechanistic explanations remains a central challenge in materials research. Here we establish PSM-Bench, an 800-question benchmark developed by perovskite researchers to evaluate scientific reasoning in perovskite photovoltaics. We also introduce OpenPerov, an expert-informed language-model framework that learns from expert-calibrated evidence records reconstructed from 4,035 training articles; these records link experimental strategies, controls and observations to mechanistic interpretations. Structured-evidence adaptation outperformed conventional question-answer training, and OpenPerov Flash ranked first among 13 closed-book systems. OpenPerov Pro raised Scientific Mastery further, from 87.6 to 89.1, by revising selected passages with retrieved evidence. On questions derived from subsequent studies, both models also outscored expert-authored answers. In an experimental test of self-assembled monolayer design, OpenPerov selected a K analogue that outperformed the Na analogue preferred by experts. Devices incorporating the selected contact reached a power conversion efficiency of 27.05% and retained 96.74% of their initial efficiency after 1,000 h of dark thermal ageing at 85 $^\circ$C. These results show that reconstructed scientific reasoning provides an effective basis for building domain models that interpret experiments and inform materials design.

infographic.engineering_relevance: Devices using the selected contact achieved 27.05% power conversion efficiency and retained 96.74% of initial efficiency after 1,000 hours of dark thermal ageing at 85°C.

title: Dynamic Molecular Transformation Mediated Crystallization Regulation and Interface Passivation in Tin Based Perovskite Solar Cells
authors: Ying Tang, Zuhong Zhang, Hongzhuo Wu, Zhihao Li, Zhenhuang Su, Yonggang Yang
abstract: Tin-based perovskites are promising candidates for lead-free photovoltaics but suffer from labile Sn$^{2+}$ coordination, rapid crystallization, and severe interfacial defects. Here, we develop a dynamic molecular transformation using 1-acetylpiperazine (PX) to regulate crystallization and interface chemistry simultaneously. During nucleation and growth, the carbonyl group coordinates with Sn$^{2+}$ to stabilize precursor complexes, moderate supersaturation, and enable controlled crystal growth. Upon annealing, PX undergoes in situ molecular transformation, suggested to form amidinium-functionalized species that preferentially occupy surface A-site vacancies, forming a passivation layer and suppressing nonradiative recombination. This coupled bulk-to-interface evolution yields compact, highly crystalline films with improved optoelectronic quality. Devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 15.18% and retain 94.1% of initial efficiency after 500 h of continuous illumination. This work demonstrates a dynamic molecular engineering approach integrating crystallization control and interface passivation, providing a pathway toward efficient and stable lead-free perovskite photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: 1-acetylpiperazine (PX) couples crystallization control with annealing-induced interface passivation to improve lead-free tin perovskite solar cells.
infographic.engineering_relevance: A dynamically transforming additive offers a route to denser, more crystalline absorber films with fewer interfacial defects and improved operational stability.

title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
authors: Zixu Huang, Julisa Juarez, Akash Dasgupta, David S. Ginger
abstract: Buried interfaces play a critical role in the operational stability of perovskite optoelectronic devices, yet remain challenging to probe non-destructively. Here, we demonstrate a multiwavelength photoluminescence-based approach exploiting the wavelength-dependent absorption of perovskites, enabling fast, and non-destructive probing of depth-sensitive degradation behavior of perovskite devices under operational conditions. Using ultraviolet (UV) light-soaking with different indium tin oxide (ITO) modifiers as a test case, we employ wide-field photoluminescence (PL) imaging, time-resolved photoluminescence (trPL) and ideality factor measurements with different wavelength excitation to characterize degradation behavior of both perovskite thin films and photovoltaic devices under UV soaking. Using only nondestructive characterization, we show that UV-induced degradation in p-i-n perovskite solar cells occurs preferentially at the HTL interface, adversely affecting device stability, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests. Our results also show that modifying the buried interface with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane reduces UV-induced damage at the buried interface, thus improving the UV stability of both perovskite films and devices. This work establishes a fast, non-destructive strategy to screen depth-dependent degradation in perovskite devices, offering insights for interface design and stability optimization.

infographic.key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage concentrated near the buried hole-transport-layer interface in p-i-n perovskite solar cells.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive degradation screening can guide interface design, with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification reducing buried-interface damage and improving UV stability.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe different depths.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL and ideality-factor measurements.

title: Humidity-modulated Ostwald Step Rule in $\rm FAPbI_3$ Martensitic Transitions
authors: Ping Tuo, Ju Li
abstract: Experimental observations reveal a dual role of moisture in $\rm FAPbI_3$ phase transitions. During fabrication at high temperatures, humidity improves the quality of the perovskite ($α$ phase) films, whereas at low service temperatures, humidity accelerates degradation of the photoactive $α$ phase into the photo-inactive hexagonal $δ$ phase. Despite extensive experimental evidence, the microscopic mechanisms by which moisture modulates phase stability and transition pathways remain unknown. Here, using large-scale atomistic simulations powered by an ab initio machine-learned potential, we reproduce the experimentally observed increase in the $δ$-to-$α$ transition temperature under increased humidity. Our simulations reveal a layered metastable intermediate along the Burgers transition pathway that exhibits a strong affinity for water. The competing water uptake of this intermediate and the $δ$ phase governs the humidity dependence of transition kinetics. These findings elucidate the dual role of moisture in perovskite phase transitions and demonstrate how environmental species can stabilize metastable intermediates and reshape transition pathways, providing an environment-dependent perspective on Ostwald's step rule.

infographic.key_insight: Humidity reshapes FAPbI₃ phase-transition pathways through competing water uptake by the δ phase and a water-affine layered metastable intermediate.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Understanding moisture-dependent transitions could help optimize perovskite film fabrication while limiting humidity-driven degradation during solar-cell operation.

Analysis of a layered metastable intermediate along the Burgers transition pathway

title: Periodic Trends in Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energies Across Binary Main-Group Metal Oxides
authors: Manish Kumar, Bridget S. Ferris, Avital Isakov, Robert B. Wexler
abstract: The function of oxide materials, from solid-oxide fuel cells to solar thermochemical fuel production, depends on their oxygen vacancies. Their formation energetics have been mapped systematically for ternary perovskites, but reported values for the binary oxides, their conceptual and thermochemical building blocks, remain scattered across studies with differing computational methods. Here we report a systematic r$^2$SCAN density functional theory survey of neutral oxygen vacancy formation energies across 39 binary main-group metal oxide polymorphs spanning groups 1, 2, 13, 14, and 15, using the ShakeNBreak method to locate reconstructed defect ground states. The formation energies span 8 eV and decrease down each group and, for most multivalent cations, with increasing oxidation state. Both trends follow the reducibility of the cation. An interpretable crystal feature model is fit to these energies; its inputs are properties of the pristine bulk, with the reduction potential alternatively taken from tabulated thermochemistry. Retaining only its two dominant descriptors, the crystal reduction potential and the band gap, the model reproduces the formation energies with a held-out mean absolute error of 0.31 eV, lower than that of its four-descriptor parent model for transition-metal perovskites. The bond-breaking and stability terms of the full Born-Haber fit prove statistically null for the binary oxides, and the largest residuals identify the hosts where electron accommodation departs from the cation-reduction picture that the descriptors encode. The dataset provides a benchmark for machine-learning interatomic potentials, and the model estimates vacancy formation energies of main-group oxides from bulk properties alone.

infographic.key_insight: Neutral oxygen vacancy formation energies in binary main-group metal oxides are largely explained by two bulk descriptors: crystal reduction potential and band gap.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The model can help screen oxide materials for vacancy-sensitive energy applications without explicit defect calculations, though solar-cell performance was not evaluated.

title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
authors: Lijun Chen, Sitong Zhao, Gaukhar Nigmetova, David Garcia Romero, Matteo Pitaro, Sofia Lerda
abstract: Interfacial nonradiative recombination limits tin-lead perovskite photovoltaics. Here we show that neutral ethylenediamine chelates undercoordinated metals at tin-rich surfaces, weakens metal-iodide bonds, and removes excess tin, reconstructing the surface towards a stoichiometric tin-to-lead ratio. In contrast, protonated ethylenediammonium iodide initially passivates undercoordinated metal sites before undergoing defect-assisted deprotonation. Atomistic simulations reveal that subsurface iodide vacancies promote iodide migration and lower the energetic cost of deprotonation. Ethylenediamine-induced reconstruction produces stronger n-type surface character, facilitates electron extraction into C60, and suppresses interfacial nonradiative recombination, enabling methylammonium-free solar cells with a power conversion efficiency of 25.86%. Together, these distinct surface reaction pathways and the defect-assisted evolution of the passivating species underscore the importance of understanding perovskite surface chemistry for the rational design of molecular passivation strategies.

infographic.key_insight: Ethylenediamine reconstructs tin-rich tin–lead perovskite surfaces toward a stoichiometric tin-to-lead ratio, improving electron extraction and reducing interfacial recombination.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Controlling molecular protonation and surface defects offers a route to more efficient methylammonium-free perovskite solar cells.

title: Competing Octahedral Tilting and $B$-Site Off-Centering Govern the Phase Diagram of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ Perovskite Alloys
authors: Apinya Ngoipala, Erik Fransson, Paul Erhart, Julia Wiktor
abstract: Lead-free halide perovskites based on Ge and Sn avoid the toxicity of Pb, but the two cations favor different structural distortions. The stereochemically active Ge $4s^2$ lone pair drives polar $B$-site off-centering, whereas the larger Sn$^{2+}$ cation favors octahedral tilting. Here, we map how these two instabilities compete across the full composition range of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations with a charge-aware machine-learned interatomic potential trained on hybrid-functional data. At low temperature the alloy exhibits a morphotropic phase boundary between $x=0.60$ and $0.65$ that separates a ferroelectric monoclinic $Cc$ phase from a monoclinic $P2_1$ phase with mixed antipolar and polar off-centering, with both the tilt pattern and the off-centering order changing discontinuously. The composition-temperature phase diagram reproduces the known transition sequences and temperatures of both end members and reveals an intermediate tetragonal $I4/mcm$ phase near the boundary that has no counterpart in either parent compound. Above the transition temperatures the $B$ cations remain locally off-centered but orientationally disordered. The structural transition at the boundary causes a jump in the band gap at low temperature, whereas at $350$ K the gap decreases smoothly with Sn content. These results establish $B$-site mixing as a means to tune polar and rotational order in lead-free halide perovskites.

infographic.key_insight: Competing Ge-driven polar off-centering and Sn-favored octahedral tilting create a low-temperature phase boundary between Sn fractions x = 0.60 and 0.65 in lead-free CsGe₁₋ₓSnₓBr₃.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Ge/Sn mixing offers a route to tune structural order and band gaps in lead-free perovskites, with potential relevance to solar-cell absorber design.
method: Train a charge-aware machine-learned interatomic potential on hybrid-functional data.

infographic.paper_title: Competing Octahedral Tilting and $B$-Site Off-Centering Govern the Phase Diagram of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ Perovskite Alloys

title: Amorphous selenium-alloyed TeOx thin-film solar cells
authors: Zhaoheng Ling, Linqu Luo, Chrysa Aivalioti, Temur Maksudov, Mengxi Zhang, Theodoulos Kalogerakis
abstract: Tellurium dioxide (TeO$_2$) is a wide-bandgap oxide with attractive processing versatility and emerging p-type semiconducting behaviour, making it a promising material system for optoelectronic and photovoltaic applications. However, TeO$_2$-derived thin films prepared by scalable manufacturing processes, such as vacuum sublimation, can contain residual metallic Te$^0$ species that introduce trap states, limit hole transport, and promote carrier recombination. Here, we demonstrate a selenium alloying strategy to control the defect chemistry of vacuum-sublimed TeO$_x$ films. TeO$_2$:Se powder mixtures (90:10~wt\%) were thermally evaporated and subsequently annealed in air at 225~$^\circ$C for up to 9~h, yielding amorphous TeO$_x$:Se films with an optical bandgap of 0.98~eV under optimised conditions. Structural, chemical, optical, and electrical analyses show that prolonged annealing promotes Se redistribution, suppresses residual Te$^0$ to approximately 0.4\%, reduces the film's surface roughness, and shifts the valence-band edge. To evaluate the potential of TeO$_x$:Se for photovoltaic applications, we fabricated thin-film solar cells with an ITO/ZnO/TeO$_x$:Se/MoO$_x$/Ag architecture. Devices based on an 80~nm TeO$_x$:Se active layer annealed for 9~h exhibit optimal performance, with broadband photocurrent generation from 300 to 1000~nm, yielding an open-circuit voltage of 0.50~V, a short-circuit current density of 8.50~mA~cm$^{-2}$, a fill factor of 0.44, and a maximum power conversion efficiency of approximately 1.87\%. These results establish selenium-alloyed TeO$_x$ as a viable oxide-derived absorber for thin-film photovoltaics and highlight chemical-state control as an effective route for improving photovoltaic performance.

infographic.key_insight: Selenium alloying and air annealing suppress residual metallic tellurium in amorphous TeOx films, enabling thin-film solar cells with approximately 1.87% peak efficiency.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Chemical-state control offers a route to improving oxide-derived photovoltaic absorbers made by vacuum deposition.

title: Analytical Framework Relating Capacitance-Frequency Measurements and Hysteresis in Perovskite Solar Cells
authors: Manjeet Kumar, Changzeng Ding, Mathias Nyman, Yongqi Sun, Chang-Qi Ma, Ronald Österbacka
abstract: Mobile ion migration strongly influences the electrical response and current-voltage hysteresis of perovskite solar cells. However, quantitative determination of ionic transport parameters typically requires transient measurements, extensive numerical simulations, and/or fitting procedures involving multiple uncertain parameters. Here, we present an analytical model that establishes a direct relationship between capacitance-frequency (C-f) characteristics and ionic transport properties in perovskite solar cells, while accounting for interlayer effects. The model describes the transition from the ion-screened depletion capacitance at low frequencies to the geometric capacitance at high frequencies and demonstrates that the characteristic transition frequency provides a direct measure of the dielectric relaxation time for ions. Furthermore, the model establishes a quantitative connection between C-f characteristics and scan-rate-dependent current-voltage hysteresis, enabling prediction of the scan-rate window in which maximum hysteresis occurs. Drift-diffusion simulations show excellent agreement with the analytical predictions over wide ranges of ion density, ion mobility, transport-layer mobility and doping concentration. Experimental measurements confirm the predicted correlation between capacitance and hysteresis. By providing a direct, physically transparent, and computationally efficient route for extracting ionic transport parameters from routine impedance measurements, this work offers a practical tool for quantifying ion migration and understanding dynamic phenomena in perovskite solar cells.

infographic.key_insight: An analytical model links capacitance–frequency measurements to ionic relaxation and predicts the scan-rate window of maximum current–voltage hysteresis in perovskite solar cells.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Routine impedance measurements could provide a physically transparent, computationally efficient route to quantify ion migration and interpret device hysteresis.

title: Energy system device sizing under closed-loop operation with imperfect forecasts
authors: Cara Koepele, Kevin Wallington, Georgios Mavromatidis, John Lygeros
abstract: The value of renewable energy devices depends on their operation, which must adapt to weather and demand using limited, imperfect forecasts that update over time. Conventional energy systems planning practices assume unlimited foresight in a single-level formulation, potentially leading to long-term investment in suboptimal device sizes. Accounting for realistic operation corresponds to a bi-level problem: the upper level selects device sizes, while the lower level contains closed-loop operation under evolving forecasts. We solve this problem using backpropagation MPC (BP-MPC), a gradient-based method, with a deterministic MPC as the lower-level controller. Using forecast errors generated by a parameterized martingale model of forecast evolution, we investigate how forecast accuracy affects the benefits of operation-aware energy systems planning and the resulting device sizes. In a case study of an energy system comprising photovoltaics, a battery, a heat pump, and thermal storage with uncertain weather and energy demands, accounting for closed-loop operation yields higher average cost savings as forecast error increases. The resulting designs achieve these savings by progressively shifting investment from battery storage to solar generation and thermal storage, which buffers forecast mismatches.

infographic.key_insight: Sizing energy devices for closed-loop operation with imperfect forecasts delivers greater average cost savings as forecast error increases, shifting investment from batteries toward photovoltaics and thermal storage.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Energy-system planners should account for forecast-driven control when sizing solar generation and storage rather than assume perfect foresight.
method: Formulate device sizing and closed-loop operation as a bi-level optimization problem.
Use backpropagation MPC with a deterministic MPC controller to optimize device sizes.

infographic.watch_item: The abstract reports one system case study; generalization to other configurations and real-world forecast errors remains to be established.
infographic.paper_title: Energy system device sizing under closed-loop operation with imperfect forecasts

title: MOTIF: LLM-Defined Material Taxonomies for OOD Property Prediction via Invariant Feature Selection
authors: Gwangseon Jang, Sieun Yun, Dong Ho Lee, Kyong-Ha Lee, Chanuk Lim, Jin Woo Choi
abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization remains a central challenge in materials property prediction, where models must extrapolate to novel chemistries beyond the training distribution. While large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong scientific reasoning, their direct use for quantitative prediction remains limited. To address this, we systematically evaluate multiple roles for LLM assistance, finding that only taxonomy-based grouping consistently improves OOD generalization over a strong kNN+GBT baseline. Building on this, we here propose MOTIF, a framework that leverages LLMs not as predictors, but as generators of candidate taxonomies that partition materials into chemically meaningful environments. These taxonomies are evaluated via training-only pseudo-OOD validation, and only those that improve generalization are retained. Invariant feature selection is then applied within each accepted taxonomy, followed by gated aggregation across taxonomies. We evaluate on 2D halide perovskites, where bandgap prediction must generalize across distinct organic spacer families. On this benchmark, MOTIF reduces mean OOD MAE from 0.122 to 0.111 eV. Under a frozen dev/test protocol, the deployable configuration further improves errors from 0.123 to 0.117 eV (electronic bandgap) and from 0.181 to 0.173 eV (optical bandgap). Beyond this primary task, we validate transferability across additional materials datasets, including 3D perovskite solar cell efficiencies and Matbench benchmarks with structure-based splits. Across domains, MOTIF consistently improves robustness under distribution shift, outperforming expert-defined groupings, rule-based heuristics, and clustering baselines, while remaining competitive with strong classical selection methods. These results demonstrate that LLMs are most effective not as predictors, but as tools for discovering structure in data.

infographic.key_insight: MOTIF improves materials-property prediction under distribution shift by using LLMs to propose chemical taxonomies, rather than predict numerical properties directly.
infographic.engineering_relevance: More robust prediction for unfamiliar material families could support perovskite screening, with transferability also evaluated on 3D perovskite solar-cell efficiencies.
method: Generate candidate material taxonomies with LLMs.
Retain taxonomies that improve training-only pseudo-OOD validation.
Select invariant features within accepted taxonomies and combine predictions through gated aggregation.
infographic.evidence_signal: On 2D halide perovskites, mean OOD bandgap MAE fell from 0.122 to 0.111 eV; frozen dev/test evaluation also showed electronic and optical bandgap improvements.
infographic.watch_item: Benefits depend on taxonomy quality and validation design; the abstract does not quantify solar-cell efficiency gains.
infographic.paper_title: MOTIF: LLM-Defined Material Taxonomies for OOD Property Prediction via Invariant Feature Selection

title: A Hybrid TFT-NBEATS Framework for Robust Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
authors: Shafi Bin Sultan, Sabik Bin Sultan, Mohammad Tajrian Arafat Alvi, Rayhanul Islam Sony, Abdulah Al Numan
abstract: Accurate multi-horizon photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for grid stability, energy scheduling, and the efficient operation of PVbatterygrid systems. However, existing models often fail to jointly capture short-term variability and long-term temporal patterns, while lacking unified multi-horizon capability and interpretability. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel hybrid deep learning framework that integrates a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) and N-BEATS within an attention-based fusion architecture. The proposed model leverages TFT to learn short-term temporal dependencies and dynamic feature importance, while N-BEATS captures long-term trend and seasonal components through interpretable basis decomposition. An adaptive attention mechanism dynamically fuses both branches, enabling balanced multi-scale learning. The framework simultaneously generates forecasts for 30-minute, 2-hour, 6-hour, 12-hour, and 24-hour horizons within a single unified pipeline. The model is evaluated using multi-year real-world datasets from the Desert Knowledge Australia Solar Centre (DKASC). Experimental results demonstrate superior performance over statistical, machine learning, and deep learning baselines. The proposed model achieves RMSE values of 42.35, 46.27, 52.29, and 48.11 across the 20162017, 2023, 2024, and 20252026 datasets, respectively, corresponding to a 3540% reduction compared to the best baseline (TFT). Additionally, MAPE remains below 5% across all datasets, indicating high predictive accuracy and stability. The model also provides interpretability through attention visualization and trendseasonality decomposition, and is deployed on a cloud-based platform for real-time forecasting. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework is robust, interpretable, and suitable for practical renewable energy applications.

infographic.key_insight: An attention-fused TFT–N-BEATS model jointly forecasts PV power across five horizons, with reported RMSE reductions of 35–40% versus TFT.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Multi-horizon forecasts could support grid scheduling and PV–battery operation, while attention and trend–seasonality views aid interpretation.
method: TFT models short-term dependencies and dynamic feature importance.
N-BEATS decomposes longer-term trends and seasonality.
Adaptive attention fuses both branches for 30-minute, 2-hour, 6-hour, 12-hour, and 24-hour forecasts.
infographic.evidence_signal: On multi-year DKASC datasets, the abstract reports RMSE values of 42.35–52.29 and MAPE below 5%; RMSE units and horizon-specific results are not provided.
infographic.watch_item: Generalization beyond DKASC remains unestablished; this is PV power forecasting research, not a perovskite cell-materials study.
infographic.paper_title: A Hybrid TFT-NBEATS Framework for Robust Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Power Forecasting

title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
authors: Mahmoud Samadpour, Alireza Fathi Beiraghvandi, Kazem Meraji, Tristan Sachsenweger Ballantyne, Fuxiang Ji, Mahdi Mohammadi
abstract: Surface morphology is widely considered an indicator of thin-film quality, with smoother films generally expected to exhibit more uniform optoelectronic properties. Here, we demonstrate that substantial surface evolution does not necessarily lead to increased electronic heterogeneity in mixed-dimensional perovskite heterostructures. We investigate how low-dimensional Ruddlesden-Popper capping layers derived from the sterically hindered 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium cation affect the spatial distributions of photoluminescence (PL) characteristics and quasi-Fermi level splitting (QFLS) in 3D perovskites. By combining statistical atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis with confocal, spatially resolved PL spectroscopy, we correlate surface topography with microscale optoelectronic properties. Although capping increases surface roughness and height asymmetry, it does not increase electronic inhomogeneity. Instead, the heterostructures exhibit enhanced PL, reduced non-radiative recombination, and improved spatial uniformity of radiative QFLS compared with pristine 3D films. Under accelerated aging, this contrast becomes more pronounced: pristine films develop substantial spatial fluctuations in emission and QFLS, whereas capped heterostructures largely preserve their optoelectronic homogeneity. These findings indicate that the low-dimensional capping layer suppresses aging-induced optoelectronic disorder, demonstrating that electronic uniformity can be maintained despite morphological irregularity. This decoupling provides a design principle for developing durable, high-performance perovskite photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: Low-dimensional perovskite capping increases surface roughness while preserving electronic uniformity, demonstrating that morphology and optoelectronic quality can be decoupled.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Capping layers offer a route to more durable perovskite photovoltaics and show why surface smoothness alone is an insufficient quality metric.
method: Cap 3D perovskites with Ruddlesden–Popper layers derived from 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium.
Combine statistical AFM with confocal spatially resolved photoluminescence and quasi-Fermi level splitting analysis.
Compare pristine and capped films before and after accelerated aging.
infographic.evidence_signal: Despite greater roughness and height asymmetry, capped films showed enhanced photoluminescence, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting, largely retaining optoelectronic homogeneity during aging.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative effect sizes, aging conditions, or device-level efficiency results, limiting assessment of practical performance gains.
infographic.paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures

title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
authors: Mahesh Eledath-Changarath, Jesús Ortiga-Fibla, Andrés F. Gualdrón-Reyes, Jesús Rodríguez-Romero, Iván Mora-Seró, Ana Cros
abstract: Long-term stability remains a critical challenge limiting the photovoltaic and optoelectronic applications of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites. In these materials, the choice of the organic spacer plays a key role not only in enhancing environmental stability, but also in determining their structural characteristics and carrier dynamics. Here, we present an environmental photo- and thermal-stability analysis of BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 two-dimensional lead halide perovskites by means of confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy techniques. We have investigated two different organic spacers, n-butylammonium (BA) and 2-phenylethylammonium (PEA), which provide comparable room-temperature luminescence in freshly exfoliated perovskite nanoflakes and degrade similarly through the removal of organic components and fast crystal phase decomposition into PbI2 and Pb0. However, we observed that the PEA organic cation significantly improves crystal morphology and suppresses lattice defects, resulting in slower degradation and enhanced resistance to light and thermal stress under ambient conditions. Our findings indicate that structural and chemical engineering, along with surface passivation and encapsulation strategies, are essential for achieving long-term stability in two-dimensional halide perovskite devices. Nevertheless, optimizing the balance between stability and device performance remains a critical consideration.

infographic.key_insight: PEA spacers improve crystal morphology and suppress lattice defects, slowing ambient light- and heat-induced degradation compared with BA spacers in two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Spacer selection offers a route to more stable perovskite devices but should complement surface passivation and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA₂PbI₄ and PEA₂PbI₄ perovskite nanoflakes.
Evaluated light and thermal stability under ambient conditions.
Probed degradation using confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
infographic.evidence_signal: Freshly exfoliated samples showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, while PEA-based crystals degraded more slowly despite both materials losing organic components and decomposing into PbI₂ and metallic Pb.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative lifetime or device-efficiency results, so improved material stability should not be equated with demonstrated solar-cell durability.
infographic.paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites

title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
authors: Ethan Berger, Erik Fransson, Apinya Ngoipala, Lucas Svensson, Priyanka Deswal, Mehmet Baskurt
abstract: Perovskites have been studied for a wide range of applications, from oxide-based ferroelectrics to halide-perovskite photovoltaics. Despite their diverse functionalities, these materials share strong lattice anharmonicity arising from structural instabilities such as polar off-centering and octahedral tilting. These anharmonic distortions strongly influence the low-frequency vibrational response and can be observed in infrared (IR) and Raman spectra. However, low-frequency IR and Raman signatures are typically investigated separately, hindering the development of a unified understanding of vibrational spectroscopy across perovskite classes. In this work, we use machine-learning-based molecular dynamics to simulate the IR and Raman spectra of oxide perovskites (SrTiO$_3$ and BaTiO$_3$), halide perovskites (CsPbBr$_3$, CsSnBr$_3$, and CsGeBr$_3$) and double halide perovskites (Cs$_2$AgAlBr$_6$ and Cs$_2$AgBiBr$_6$). By comparing materials exhibiting polar, tilt-driven and mixed instabilities, we find that polar off-centering leads to enhanced low-frequency IR and dielectric responses, whereas nonpolar modes, particularly octahedral tilting, are associated with Raman central peaks. The strength of the low-frequency features also depends on how strongly the underlying modes couple to polarization or dielectric susceptibility. Finally, we show that the dynamics of these instabilities play an important role, with slow polar reorientations shifting the dielectric response to very low frequencies and overdamped tilting modes producing persistent Raman central peaks. These results establish a unified framework connecting low-frequency IR and Raman spectra to the symmetry, coupling and dynamics of their underlying anharmonic lattice instabilities.

infographic.key_insight: Across perovskites, polar off-centering enhances low-frequency infrared and dielectric responses, while nonpolar octahedral tilting is associated with Raman central peaks.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Connecting spectral features to lattice instabilities can guide interpretation of vibrational measurements in perovskite solar-cell materials.
method: Simulate infrared and Raman spectra using machine-learning-based molecular dynamics.
Compare seven oxide, halide and double-halide perovskites.
Relate spectral features to instability symmetry, coupling strength and dynamics.
infographic.evidence_signal: Simulations across seven materials link slow polar reorientations to very-low-frequency dielectric responses and overdamped tilting to persistent Raman central peaks.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative accuracy benchmarks or solar-cell device tests, so photovoltaic performance benefits remain unestablished.
infographic.paper_title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites

title: Benchmark for Structured Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Perovskite Photovoltaics
authors: Qiwei Han, Chi Zhou, Gaoxiang Yuan
abstract: While retrieval-augmented language models increasingly serve as literature assistants in the physical sciences, existing benchmarks evaluate them primarily on qualitative text overlap or through model-based scoring rather than against verified experimental ground truth. In experimental materials disciplines such as perovskite photovoltaics, however, the most critical inquiries are inherently quantitative and aggregate measurements across dozens or hundreds of papers. Here, we present a quantitative question-answering benchmark where all 755 ground-truth answers are computed directly from 45,441 measured device records (40,889 human-curated records through 2021 and 4,552 records extracted from 2022-2026 literature). Benchmarking six retrieval architectures over 158,274 passages from 25,662 papers using an open 14B model on a single 24 GB GPU, standard passage retrieval tops out at 16-23% accuracy (compared to 1.6-6.5% zero-shot). In contrast, equipping the language model with read-only SQL execution over the structured device table elevates accuracy to 51.5% on historical and 50.8% on prospective literature -- a 33.01.8 percentage-point advantage over hybrid text retrieval. Aggregate queries spanning extrema, distributions, and filtered record counts prove virtually unsolvable via text retrieval alone, demonstrating that systematic table extraction is an operational prerequisite for literature-scale quantitative inquiry.

infographic.key_insight: Giving a language model read-only SQL access to structured perovskite device data raised quantitative question-answering accuracy to about 51%, versus 16–23% with passage retrieval.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Literature-scale comparisons of solar-cell measurements benefit from validated device tables and executable queries, not text retrieval alone.
method: Compute 755 ground-truth answers directly from measured device records.
Benchmark six retrieval architectures with an open 14B model on one 24 GB GPU.
Compare passage retrieval with read-only SQL access for quantitative queries.
infographic.evidence_signal: Evaluation used 45,441 device records and 158,274 passages from 25,662 papers; SQL-enabled accuracy reached 51.5% on historical and 50.8% on prospective literature.
infographic.watch_item: Accuracy remains near 51%, and deployment depends on reliable extraction and maintenance of structured device data.
infographic.paper_title: Benchmark for Structured Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Perovskite Photovoltaics

title: Stable AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
authors: Shiling Dong, Yongjie Wang, Hae-Jun Seok, Mengyuan Huang, Edward Newton, Der Ying Chen
abstract: AgBiS2 has rapidly risen in efficiency as single-junction photovoltaics (PVs), but its potential for tandem PVs is unexplored. Herein, we perform optical modeling based on the experimental absorption spectrum of AgBiS2, revealing that, as the NIR sub-cell, efficiencies exceeding 47.9% are achievable in triple-junction tandems, superseding tandems using Pb/Sn perovskite NIR cells (44.2%). However, fulfilling this potential requires overcoming the limited transport properties of AgBiS2 nanocrystal films, which constrains film thicknesses to only 30-50 nm, severely restricting NIR response. A solution-phase ligand exchange process is herein developed, allowing one-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals that maintain efficient charge-carrier extraction despite an order of magnitude increase in film thickness. These films enable 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with visible-light-absorbing lead-halide perovskite sub-cells, and monolithic tandems successfully demonstrating voltage addition. AgBiS2 PVs have high stability, retaining >90% of the original efficiency after 3 months of storage in dry air without encapsulation. This work establishes the significant potential of AgBiS2 as a stable and scalable NIR absorber for tandem PVs.

infographic.key_insight: Solution-phase ligand exchange enables thicker, charge-extracting AgBiS2 nanocrystal films for stable near-infrared tandem solar cells.
infographic.engineering_relevance: One-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 offers a potentially scalable route to near-infrared sub-cells paired with visible-light-absorbing perovskites.
method: Model tandem performance using the experimental AgBiS2 absorption spectrum.
Use solution-phase ligand exchange to passivate nanocrystals and increase usable film thickness tenfold.
Integrate AgBiS2 with lead-halide perovskites in four-terminal and monolithic tandems.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports 24.0% four-terminal tandem efficiency, voltage addition in monolithic tandems, and >90% efficiency retention after three months in dry air without encapsulation; triple-junction efficiencies exceeding 47.9% are modeled, not demonstrated.
infographic.watch_item: Dry-air storage stability does not establish durability under illumination, heat, or humidity, and the modeled triple-junction potential remains experimentally unverified.
infographic.paper_title: Stable AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
